interface.signature: def fractionToDecimal(numerator: int, denominator: int) -> str:

preconditions.description: Both numerator and denominator are integers within the range [1, 2000].
Denominator is never zero (implicitly guaranteed by constraints).

postconditions.expression: return_value == str(numerator // denominator) if numerator % denominator == 0 else return_value
postconditions.description: If the numerator is divisible by the denominator, the output is the integer quotient as a string.

postconditions.expression: '.' in return_value or return_value == str(numerator // denominator)
postconditions.description: The output is either an integer string (if no remainder) or a decimal string with a decimal point.

postconditions.expression: all(c in '0123456789.-()' for c in return_value)
postconditions.description: The output string contains only digits, '.', '-', and '()' for repeating parts.

postconditions.expression: any('(' in return_value and ')' in return_value) if numerator % denominator != 0 else False
postconditions.description: If there is a fractional part, repeating digits are enclosed in parentheses exactly once.

postconditions.expression: return_value == str(numerator / denominator) if numerator % denominator == 0 else (return_value == str(numerator / denominator).rstrip('0').rstrip('.'))
postconditions.description: The output string represents the exact decimal value of the fraction, with trailing zeros and decimal point removed if no fractional part remains.
